technical_and_design_decisions: Use the repository's existing acceptance-test framework, build conventions, and test language rather than introducing a new test technology.
Exercise each module through its public configuration and runtime interfaces, treating the tests as black-box acceptance tests.
Use deterministic local fixtures and temporary directories for file-based behavior such as shell, timestampfile, and spark-app tests.
Use a local mock or containerized test double for external Splunk communication so CI does not depend on a live Splunk environment.
Keep tests isolated, repeatable, and safe for parallel or repeated CI execution by cleaning up temporary resources and using unique test data.
Add the tests to the existing CI test task and preserve the current default build behavior unless the repository requires a separate acceptance-test profile.
assumptions: The repository already contains an acceptance-test harness, build system, module documentation, and reusable test utilities.
The implementation of all eight target modules already exists; this increment adds acceptance coverage rather than production functionality.
No new product requirements, API changes, or broad refactoring are required.
Acceptance tests can run locally in CI without privileged infrastructure, except for lightweight local processes or containers.
Existing CI configuration can be modified by one developer and has a functioning Java build environment compatible with the project.
A workday represents one productive developer day, including coding, test execution, debugging, and review-ready cleanup.
The estimates include normal implementation and debugging but exclude major defects in the existing modules, unavailable external infrastructure, and independent code-review time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the repository structure, existing acceptance tests, module interfaces, build profiles, test utilities, and CI entry points; define the coverage and fixture approach for all requested modules.
Create or adapt common test data, temporary resource handling, process lifecycle utilities, configuration helpers, and reusable assertions needed by the eight acceptance-test suites.
Implement acceptance scenarios for the null sink, including representative input, configuration, successful execution, and verification that records are handled without producing unintended output.
Implement acceptance scenarios for rich_gauge, covering representative gauge data, configuration, execution, and validation of the emitted or persisted gauge results.
Implement acceptance scenarios verifying router configuration, routing decisions for representative records, handling of unmatched or alternate routes where supported, and resulting outputs.
Implement acceptance scenarios for shell command execution, input propagation, output or side-effect verification, exit-status handling, and safe temporary command/test resources.
Implement acceptance scenarios for Splunk configuration and event delivery using a deterministic local mock or containerized service, including payload and error-path validation.
Implement acceptance scenarios for throughput-sampler configuration, sampling behavior, representative input volume, and verification of the resulting sampled or reported data.
Implement acceptance scenarios for spark-app using a local or embedded test execution mode, controlled input fixtures, job completion checks, and deterministic output validation.
Implement acceptance scenarios for timestampfile, including input and timestamp-file setup, job execution, timestamp update or output verification, and repeatable cleanup.
Register all acceptance suites in the appropriate CI build path, validate execution on a clean environment, diagnose intermittent or environment-specific failures, and confirm repeatability.

activities.activity_name: Test maintenance cleanup and delivery documentation
activities.activity_description: Refine naming and assertions, remove duplicated setup, document required local/CI prerequisites, and prepare the completed increment for delivery.
